subject: Aurora Systems — post-demo compute runway, isolation & SLA next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@aurora-systems.com>, Aidan Cho <aidan.cho@aurora-systems.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-28T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: Aurora Systems — post-demo compute runway, isolation & SLA next steps

Hi Maya / Aidan —

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared record:  

Pain points you emphasized:
- Peak inference bursts during batch processing windows (evenings PST) causing 3–4x latency spikes.
- Regulatory requirement for tenant isolation (PHI in some test datasets) — you need a dedicated, VPC-isolated pool.
- Tight cost target for inference (< $0.06 / 1k tokens) for cold-started models; willing to accept higher baseline for reserved capacity if it stabilizes latency.

Goals you called out:
- Consistent p99 latency under 350ms for short chat flows (<=64 tokens).
- Ability to scale to ~150 concurrent streams during peak with <20% queuing.
- Audit logs and key management — SOC2-aligned evidence for audit.

Redwood recommendation (high level):
- Reserved dedicated pool: 8x A100-equivalent GPU slots (quantized runtime), VPC-isolated, single-region (us-west-2) with burst policy to add 2 extra GPUs for 15-minute windows.
- Autoscaling: policy tuned by request concurrency and KV cache hit rates to preserve p99s.
- SLA: 99.9% availability + latency SLO (p99) target of 350ms for pinned model variant; operational fallback to a slightly lower-cost variant on capacity constraints.

Attachments: I attached a rough capacity estimate and an initial SLA draft for your review.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Aurora to confirm expected steady-state concurrency and burst cadence (Aidan) — due: Tue 2027-02-02
2) Redwood to produce a formal sizing + pricing sheet and MOP for isolation + onboarding — (Jordan / Rishi) — target: Thu 2027-02-03
3) Security sync to review KMS and logging requirements (Monica + Aurora sec ops) — schedule next week.

If that aligns, I’ll kick off a short mutual action plan and loop in procurement.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: aurora_capacity_estimate.xlsx, redwood_sla-draft_v1.pdf

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@aurora-systems.com>

Cc: Aidan Cho <aidan.cho@aurora-systems.com>, ops@aurora-systems.com
Date: 2027-01-28T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Aurora Systems — post-demo compute runway, isolation & SLA next steps

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:  

- Concurrency: our steady-state expectation is ~60 concurrent streams, with nightly batch bursts that can push to ~180 for 30–45 minutes. The bursts are predictable (22:00–23:00 PST) and tied to ETL windows.
- Model variants: we’ll likely run two variants — a smaller local model for high-volume low-latency tasks and a larger model for higher-quality responses. We’d want both available in the dedicated pool if possible.
- Compliance: SOC2 and KMS are must-haves; we have an internal auditor who will want a copy of the audit log schema.

Questions for Redwood:  
1) Can the pool be configured to guarantee GPU affinity for the primary variant (no cold starts)?
2) What does the fallback to a lower-cost variant look like operationally (latency delta and expected quality impact)?
3) Procurement: do you support a 12-month committed contract with quarterly true-ups?

I attached our network-requirements csv and a one-page summary of the burst cadence. Will loop our procurement lead if sizing/pricing looks reasonable.

Thanks — Maya
Maya Singh | VP of Engineering, Aurora Systems
maya.singh@aurora-systems.com | +1 650-555-1299

Attachments: network-requirements.csv

Date: 2027-01-28T14:10:00-08:00

Rishi / Monica — forwarding Maya’s reply and Aurora’s attachments. Key asks: guarantee affinity for primary variant, run two pinned variants in the same dedicated pool, predictable burst cadence (22:00–23:00 PST), SOC2/KMS audit log schema.  

Action items I’d like from you:  
- Rishi: can you put together a conservative sizing + cost sheet for 8–10 reserved GPUs (including quantized runtime options) and what the burst policy would cost if they need +2 GPUs for 45 minutes? Also include fallback variant performance delta estimates.
- Monica: please prepare security onboarding checklist items we’ll need to meet Aurora’s auditor — KMS integration flow, sample audit log output, and the timeline for SOC2 evidence handoff.

I’ll draft the mutual action plan once I have those pieces; looks like procurement will get involved if the numbers look reasonable.

— Jordan

Jordan / Monica — quick engineering sizing and operational notes based on the numbers Maya provided:  

Proposed configuration (conservative):
- Reserved pool: 10x A100-equivalent GPU slots (supports 2 pinned model variants). We recommend 10 reserved to keep headroom for cache warmups and admin tasks.
- Burst policy: +2 GPUs available for up to 60 minutes per burst; billing model: 2x on-demand rate for burst minutes beyond reserved baseline.
- Model affinity: we can pin model containers to GPUs to avoid cold starts; initial warmup preloads and persistent KV cache to keep p99s low.

SLOs / SLA:
- Availability: 99.9% (standard enterprise tier)
- Latency: target p99 <= 350ms for the primary variant at <=64 tokens; secondary variant expected p99 ~450–550ms depending on prompt complexity.

Security / compliance:
- KMS: customer-managed keys supported via our KMS connector (docs attached to the checklist Monica will produce).
- Audit logs: we can export structured logs to your S3 bucket or forward to your SIEM (log schema: timestamp, request_id, model_variant, latency_ms, user_id (hashed), audit_flags).

Prov pricing note (high level):
- 12-month committed pricing supported with quarterly usage true-ups. We’ll include an option for a 6-month ramp to account for ML performance tuning.

I’ll prepare the sizing spreadsheet (with estimated monthly spend ranges, token-based forecasts, and burst cost model) and share it by end of day 2027-02-03. Monica — will hand the security checklist to you in the next email so you can attach to the MAP.

— Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
